comments.text: Bytes preceding the actual $0810 entry. After three zero bytes they contain a call to $E5A0, a CIA2 direction-register update and the first two bytes of an absolute load.
Blanks the display and installs the VIC-II defaults. Banks out the KERNAL, initializes the sound routine with A=0 and clears $CE26 and $CE27. Selects VIC bank $8000 and screen matrix $8C00.
Waits for raster $FA, then chooses the approach or pole-field update using $1AD9. The field update handles input, landing and animation before updating the panel and checking the round outcome.
At raster $FF, sets border and background to black and blanks the display. Returns after 100 successful reads of raster line zero.
Waits for raster line zero and sets $D011 to $3B to enable the bitmap display.
Sets the KERNAL input and output device numbers to 0 and 3. Copies the VIC-II preset from $ECB9, leaving display control, border and background colour unchanged.
Waits for CIA1 port A to equal $6F. A different reading clears the latch at $CE23, and accepting a press sets the latch so a held button cannot count twice.

Mutes sound and disables all sprites. On the first pass increments $1B15 and returns. On subsequent passes draws result-screen borders at $8C00 from the horizontal and paired vertical edge templates in $CF00-$CF9F.

Derives the award percentage from the saved target value and elapsed counter, subtracting the elapsed excess over 30. A result of at least 50 sets the apprentice flag. Stores the rounded-up shares of 25, 0, 53 and 52 in the apprentice training record.
The two displayed result digits written by $0BA1 as it converts the award to decimal.
Doubles the message-list number to select a pointer from $1D11. Calls $0BF1 with each message ID until the list reaches $FF.
Selects the message stream from $1D35 and uses its column and row to calculate a destination in the $8C00 character screen. The stream uses $FE to start another row and $FF to end.
Copies the three-page font from $ED80 to VIC bank 2 at $A000, sets colour RAM from the authored screen matrix at $8C00 and enables character mode before polling for fire.
Clears the matrix, copies seven common 20-character rows from $CE40, and adds the active apprentice name from $CE03 or $CE0D.

Branches on $1AD9. During the approach it reads right as $77 at CIA1 port A and uses the movement table at $1BF2. On the poles it waits for the request flag at $1B0A and distinguishes left, right and fire.

Updates the in-progress pose over three calls, copying 128 bytes on each call. The fourth applies horizontal displacement to six sprites and swaps their screen pointers to the other six-sprite buffer.
Enables all sprites, uses multicolour for the six body sprites and assigns the initial pointer values and VIC-II coordinates from the stage tables.
Patches the single target-count digit from $1AD3, then advances the four decimal timer digits. A carry into the second-highest digit increments the elapsed counter at $1AD5.
Renders the six digit fields at $1CD8–$1CDE, skipping the decimal point at $1CDA. Each digit selects eight bitmap bytes from $EF00 and writes one cell in the three HUD fields.
Sets colour cells near the bottom of the matrix. Converts the text at $1CAF through the two font pages beginning at $ED80 and $EE80, then draws the glyphs into the bitmap starting at $BE00.
Clears 64 overlapping 256-byte ranges through a pointer starting at $2000. It steps the start by 255 bytes and uses $1ADF as its outer counter.
Copies the Balance bitmap at $5800 to $A000 and the screen-colour matrix at $7800 to $8C00. Uses overlapping 256-byte passes and then clears colour RAM.
Enables raster IRQs, masks CIA1 interrupts, selects RAM under the KERNAL and installs $198A through the hardware IRQ vector.

Acknowledges the VIC-II interrupt and selects one of five raster phases by incrementing $1AE0 modulo five. The first phase sets multicolour mode and a new background, calls the phase routines and sets the next line to $30.
Balance movement and animation state. The initial values include target, timing, lane and pose progress, the obstacle counters, and the saved target and time values used by the result calculation.
Eight starting addresses for the animated bitmap section. $0E5E selects a six-row frame and reads one 64-byte section per row, stepping the source by 320.
Twenty-one initial countdown values, each set to eight. The selector at $1671 cycles through the first twelve for the obstacle-column update.
Six X and Y byte pairs written to $D000–$D00B when the chamber assembles the Balance apprentice sprites.
Four candidate 9-bit X positions for sprite 6. $0EDC chooses a position by using the CIA timer and writes the high bit through $D010. The initial position copy also uses the first three bytes.
31 pointers spaced $0180 bytes apart. The pose number at $1ADD selects the base used by the sprite copy at $1277.
Three little-endian pointers to the four-byte motion records consumed by the pose sequencer at $118F.
Motion sequence 0. Each four-byte record provides the pose and a little-endian position delta in its last two bytes. A first byte of $FF ends the sequence.
Motion sequence 1. Each four-byte record provides the pose and a little-endian position delta in its last two bytes. A first byte of $FF ends the sequence.
Motion sequence 2. Each four-byte record provides the pose and a little-endian position delta in its last two bytes. A first byte of $FF ends the sequence.
Seven pose-number and displacement-byte pairs consumed by the crouch animation at $0F46. A pose byte of $FF is the sentinel.
Nine bytes copied by $12DF to $D025–$D02D, beginning with the shared multicolour pair and ending with the seventh local sprite colour.
Four 40-byte columns of bitmap cell backups. The $12EB copier takes five rows of eight bytes per column from the original playfield before the obstacle writers change it.
Terminated label text drawn by $1829 into the bottom of the playfield. The following decimal digit fields are updated independently.
Four timer digits around a fixed decimal point and two counters. $1684 updates the timer and transfers all six digit glyphs to the bitmap.
Twenty-five consecutive little-endian multiples of 40 for positioning messages in the character matrix.
Six result-mode pointers. The dispatcher selects one from the mode byte at $CE24.
Six lists of message indices. Each $FF ends a list and returns from the result-message dispatcher.
Twelve message pointers. Entries 1 and 3 point to the same Congratulations message.
Positioned result text for loss of balance. $FE starts another positioned row and $FF terminates this message.

The Balance music service entry jumps to the voice updater at $E22C.
Clears the voice and filter state and resets the SID. Uses A to select the divider and six initial voice pointer bytes, and marks the first pass to fetch a sequence entry.

Interprets track bytes as a new track pointer, voice offsets or a repeat count. Nonnegative values select a phrase through the directory. Saves the new track position and begins the phrase. An initial $FE command instead latches the service entry to return until reinitialized.
Starts the player at voice index two or continues the current voice. The tick divider and note timers decide whether to fetch another phrase byte or step the instrument and write the active voice.
Selects the phrase using the current voice’s index. Decodes note, duration, instrument, filter, pitch override and slide commands. A zero byte returns to track processing.
Updates SID gate and envelope according to the instrument flags, resets modulation on a new note and reads the note frequency from its two byte tables. Updates the duration and saved phrase position.

Services the remaining voices by descending register index. The final voice updates the tick divider and SID mode and resonance. The filter step path reads a timed incremental cutoff command and writes $D416.

Initializes the slide when its counter is negative. Computes the interval from the difference of two note frequencies divided by the duration. Thereafter decrements the counter and adds the stored interval.
Writes a relative note lookup or a literal high frequency byte, then resumes instrument decoding. The silent branch resets the selected voice control and both envelope registers before moving on.
Uses the current instrument or the active override to select a pitch program. Applies its loop and timing fields and updates the note frequency from the program’s command.
Uses the instrument to choose a timed pulse increment program and advances that program when the countdown elapses. Adds the active increment to the saved pulse width.
Selects a fixed instrument control byte or the next byte from a control program. Applies the current voice mask and saves the program position.
Writes control, frequency, pulse width, attack/decay and sustain/release to the selected SID voice, then advances to the next voice.
